topIssues.title: warm-pool entries whose container died hold node slots forever: healthCheck() has no live caller
topIssues.author: standujar
topIssues.body:
## What happens

Warm-pool entries whose container has died stay `running` forever, hold their node slot, count against the node's allocation, and make that node permanently undrainable.

Measured on production 2026-08-06 by diffing `docker ps -a` on all nine nodes against the rows that claim them:

| | |
|---|---|
| real agent containers | 169 |
| rows claiming a container | 238 |
| **rows claiming a container that does not exist** | **77** |
| containers with no row at all | 8 (3 up since 13 July) |

Three autoscaled ccx33 nodes bought on 26, 27 and 28 July (`167.233.20.85`, `178.105.77.91`, `88.198.118.204`) hold **four such rows each**, have **zero containers**, and have read as fully allocated for ten days.

## Why nothing collects them

`WarmPoolManager.healthCheck()` probes every ready pool entry and destroys the dead ones — container *and* row, via `destroyPoolContainer` → `deleteAgent` → `deletePoolEntry`. It is exactly the missing collector, and it has **no live caller**: the only one is `/api/v1/cron/pool-health-check` on the container-control-plane, which the daemon's own comments call deprecated. The daemon's `runInfraMaintenanceCycle` runs node-health, disk, alloc-reconcile, pre-pull, autoscale, pool-drain, pool-replenish and orphan-reconcile — no pool health check.

This is the same omission as `replenish`, already documented in `provisioning-worker.ts` fifteen lines away, and nothing else can see these rows:

- **the heartbeat skips them.** `listRunning()` filters `execution_tier != 'shared'`, and `createPoolEntry` never sets `execution_tier`, so every pool row falls to the schema default `shared` — while carrying a real `node_id` and `container_name`. The docblock's premise ("shared rows are container-free by design") is false for pool rows.
- **`reconcileUnclaimable` cannot reach them.** Its candidate query ends `NOT (warmPoolRuntimeReadyConditions)` — a fully ready row is excluded by construction.
- **the orphan reconciler cannot reach them.** It starts from the Docker listing, so an empty node yields an empty candidate set.

## Why it costs servers

- `countAllocatedWorkloadsOnNode` counts non-terminal rows; `running` counts. The node reads as allocated.
- `findDrainCandidates` skips any node with `allocated > 0` — a row is treated as proof of a workload. The node can never be drained.
- `syncAllocatedCounts` runs every five minutes, armed, and re-asserts the inflated count rather than repairing it.
- `container-billing` and `agent-billing` select on `status = 'running'` with no node-side check, so **these rows are billed hourly**.

Net effect: the pool can only grow. Every phantom permanently removes a slot from `totalAvailable` and permanently disqualifies its node from drain.

## Related, not fixed here

- **The 77 rows already stranded** need the reverse reconciler — "row claims container C on node N, `docker ps` does not list it past a grace window → release the placement". No such path exists: every writer of `node_id`/`container_name` to NULL (`executeSleep`, `retireFailedWarmClaimForRetry`, `trySetProvisioning`) is triggered by a job or an error string, never by container absence.
- **`ORPHAN_RECONCILER_ENABLED` is set in no deployment config**, so the container-side reconciler has never run. It would collect the 8 rowless containers. Arming it is an ops decision — it issues `docker rm -f`.
- **`/v1/admin/docker-containers/audit`** — the ghost-container detection route — is a `501` stub.
- **`admin-infrastructure.ts` already computes the drift** and raises a `critical` alert past |2|. The three empty nodes sit at −4, so three critical alerts have been rendering for ten days with no remediation arm.
- **`processDisconnectedRecovery` is scoped `dedicated-always`**, so a `dedicated-lazy` row that flips to `disconnected` is never re-probed and holds its slot permanently — a second, quieter leak.
- **Node `capacity` looks wrong**: the autoscaler buys ccx33 and declares them 4 slots while the original nodes declared 24 are carrying 38.

topIssues.title: fix(ci): develop verify gate is red — certification-hosted fleet routing violates the HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE contract (#17812 follow-up)
topIssues.author: krutftw
topIssues.body:
## Problem

`bun run verify` is red on `develop` for every contributor as of `bc3be9cae` (#17812): `audit:hetzner-fleet-routing` throws.

Executed against the actual `develop` workflow tree (extracted via `git archive origin/develop .github/workflows`, validated with the unmodified contract script):

```text
AUDIT FAILS:
Hetzner runner routing must require explicit HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE opt-in; missing, empty, false, and noncanonical values must use a hosted runner:
certification-hosted.yml:33 (on.workflow_dispatch.inputs.runner.description): Runner pool: hosted (ubuntu-24.04) or the self-hosted hetzner-robot fleet
certification-hosted.yml:53 (jobs.hosted-certification.runs-on): ${{ inputs.runner == 'robot' && fromJSON('["self-hosted","hetzner-robot"]') || 'ubuntu-24.04' }}
```

Two distinct violations from the same commit:

1. **The `runs-on` selector is non-canonical and skips the `HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE` gate entirely.** `packages/scripts/hetzner-fleet-routing-contract.mjs` allowlists exact selectors, all var-gated, and hard-fails anything else routing to the fleet labels. Beyond the audit, the gap is behavioral: an operator dispatching `runner: robot` while the fleet is offline queues the run against zero registered runners indefinitely — the fail-safe the contract exists to guarantee.
2. **The input's `description` string trips the collector too** — it walks every YAML scalar for the trigger substrings, so the literal `hetzner-robot` in prose is flagged alongside the real selector.

Both were called out pre-merge on #17812 (review thread has the full trace); the merge landed without them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `certification-hosted.yml`'s `runs-on` composes the dispatch input **with** the `HETZNER_FLEET_ONLINE` gate, in the contract's existing composed-selector shape, so an explicit `robot` dispatch degrades to hosted when the fleet is offline instead of hanging.
- [ ] That exact selector string is added to `DIRECT_RUNNER_SELECTORS` in `hetzner-fleet-routing-contract.mjs` with a comment naming the workflow and why the input is safe (dispatch-only surface).
- [ ] The input description no longer contains collector trigger substrings.
- [ ] `node packages/scripts/hetzner-fleet-routing-contract.mjs` (the `audit:hetzner-fleet-routing` entry) passes on the result; red-on-develop / green-on-branch runs included as evidence.
- [ ] The per-dispatch `runner` choice and the 300-minute cap from #17812 are preserved — this repairs the routing contract, it does not revert the capacity fix.

topIssues.title: fix(benchmarks): execute and compute the supported meeting parity matrix
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Original issue

- Replaces and focuses #12501.
- Code PR: #13293
- Agent evidence: `.github/issue-evidence/12501-parity-matrix-report.md`

## What is blocked on a human

This is blocked on live systems and physical/simulator evidence an agent cannot supply from this workspace:

- Local fused inference runtime for local ASR + local LLM + local TTS.
- Cloud ASR/STT, LLM, and TTS provider credentials with real billing/cost logs.
- Native TalkMode STT/TTS on the supported native target.
- Browser Web Speech fallback in a real browser session.
- Offline mode with networking disabled, tested separately from degraded-network mode.
- Degraded-network mode with real network shaping and retry/dropout evidence.
- Mobile bridge/local inference on iOS or Android device/simulator with resource logs.
- Audio/video capture permission, consent, and retained artifacts for at least one desktop lane, one mobile lane, and one cloud lane.

## Exact human steps

1. Check out PR #13293 or its branch `fix/12501-parity-matrix-report` and build/deploy the latest tree before recording evidence.
2. Prepare a real `meeting-transcription-proof` manifest with the existing required sections plus the new `parity_matrix` section.
3. Use the same scenario ids and artifact schema for every non-skipped parity lane.
4. Run all nine lanes:
   - `local_asr_local_llm_local_tts`
   - `local_asr_cloud_llm_local_tts`
   - `cloud_asr_cloud_llm_cloud_tts`
   - `cloud_asr_local_llm_local_tts`
   - `native_talkmode_stt_tts`
   - `browser_web_speech_fallback`
   - `offline_mode`
   - `degraded_network_mode`
   - `mobile_bridge_local_inference`
5. For each non-skipped lane, collect WER, CER, DER, JER, cpWER, WDER, TTFA, final transcript latency, first note latency, CPU, memory, battery delta, thermal state, cloud cost, network bytes, failure rate, retry count, dropout rate, and privacy mode.
6. Generate a baseline comparison for every non-skipped lane. A lane with a regression must not be marked `pass`.
7. Mark a lane `skip` only when it is genuinely unsupported or inaccessible, and write a specific `skip_reason`. Skips are not counted as passes and keep the real report non-publishable.
8. Attach the real artifacts: matrix report, metrics JSON, baseline comparisons, device/resource logs, cloud cost/network records, backend logs, frontend console/network logs, screenshots, and audio/video walkthrough captures for desktop, mobile, and cloud coverage.
9. Run:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=packages/benchmarks/meeting-transcription-proof \
  python -m elizaos_meeting_transcription_proof \
  --lane real_product \
  --manifest /path/to/real-meeting-manifest.json \
  --output /tmp/mtp-real
```

10. Open `/tmp/mtp-real/meeting-transcription-proof-report.json` and manually inspect that all nine lanes pass, `skip_count` and `fail_count` are zero, `baseline_regression_count` is zero, and `publishable` is true.
11. Attach the reviewed report and artifacts to this issue and PR #13293.

## Work an agent can still do

- Convert human-provided artifacts into a manifest that satisfies the #13293 schema.
- Debug validator failures and make error messages clearer if the real artifacts expose gaps.
- Add regression tests for any newly discovered malformed manifests or baseline edge cases.
- Run the focused pytest suite and orchestrator smoke after human artifacts are added.
- Update the PR evidence table with exact artifact links once the human uploads them.

## Done when

- PR #13293 is merged or superseded by an equivalent implementation.
- The real `real_product` manifest validates with all nine parity lanes passing.
- Desktop, mobile, and cloud evidence artifacts are attached and manually reviewed.
- Offline mode and degraded-network mode are both exercised and reported separately.
- Skipped lanes, if any, are treated as blockers rather than passes.

topIssues.title: feat(benchmarks): add reproducible same-input Eliza and open-source baseline runners
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Parent issue: #12536
Code PR: #13213

## Human Blocker

The benchmark now enforces a baseline-comparison manifest/report contract, but real baseline proof still requires humans with approved accounts, local runtime setup, and terms review. An agent in this local environment cannot honestly run Otter/Granola/Zoom/Gemini commercial products, accept their terms, inspect account-policy limits, or run and manually review real open-source baseline outputs over production meeting media.

## Required Human Steps

1. Select one shared meeting/audio scenario and run the current Eliza production path to produce the Eliza baseline artifact.
2. Run or import terms-approved outputs for any commercial systems used: Otter-style bot, Granola-style bot-free capture, Zoom native transcript/AI Companion, Google Meet/Gemini notes, or explicit `not_run` rows with reasons.
3. Run at least one open-source baseline over the same scenario/audio, preferably WhisperX + pyannote; optionally add NeMo Sortformer if installed.
4. Attach each baseline artifact without normalizing away useful system differences: transcript, diarization, speaker labels, generated notes, decisions, action items, latency/capture metadata, and privacy/capture mode.
5. Attach Eliza artifacts for the same scenario/audio, metrics JSON, and a Markdown report comparing WER/CER, DER/JER, cpWER/WDER, speaker-name accuracy, action-item F1, decision F1, unsupported-claim rate, latency, and privacy/capture mode.
6. Add manual review notes for at least one transcript and one notes artifact per compared system.
7. Add terms/usage notes for every commercial output import, including whether automation, redistribution, or screenshots are allowed.
8. Run the real `meeting_transcription_proof` lane with the evidence manifest and link the report from PR #13213 or a follow-up PR.

## Work An Agent Can Still Do

- Validate a sanitized real manifest with `baseline_comparisons` against the benchmark CLI.
- Add deterministic regression fixtures from approved/sanitized baseline outputs.
- Summarize metric deltas and unsupported-claim/action-item discrepancies.
- Update the registry scorer or report renderer if real evidence exposes a missing comparison field.

## Done Criteria

- A real-lane report includes all required baseline comparison rows and complete evidence files.
- At least one open-source baseline is run or imported over the same scenario/audio as Eliza.
- Commercial systems are either imported with terms/usage notes or explicitly `not_run` with reasons.
- Manual review notes and metric artifacts are linked from PR #13213 or a follow-up PR.

topIssues.title: fix(benchmarks): wire meeting-intelligence generation and scoring into the real lane
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
Parent issue: #12499
Code PR: #13169

## Human Blocker

The benchmark contract and deterministic scorer are implemented, but #12499 cannot be fully closed as product proof until a human runs real meeting-intelligence flows with live model access and reviews the generated artifacts. Agents cannot honestly provide the required real meeting recordings, live LLM trajectories, or manually reviewed product artifacts from this local environment.

## Required Human Steps

1. Run the meeting transcription proof benchmark in `real_product` mode against real Zoom, Google Meet, bot-free desktop/on-device, cloud agent, and hybrid local/cloud meeting captures.
2. Generate meeting summaries, action items with owner/date, decisions, open questions, and memory/knowledge writes from a live model, not a mock provider.
3. Capture live model trajectories for generated-artifact judging: native JSONL, JSON report, raw prompts, model outputs, and judge outputs for hallucination and factuality checks.
4. Manually review every generated artifact against the source transcript spans and attach the review notes for summary factuality, action item owner/date correctness, decisions, open questions, memory entity correctness, hallucination rate, omission rate, and source grounding.
5. Attach backend structured logs, frontend console/network logs, before/after desktop and mobile screenshots, and a screen recording of the full meeting intelligence flow.
6. Inspect and attach domain artifacts: transcript artifact, generated notes/actions/decisions/questions, memory or knowledge rows before and after the meeting, retention/deletion artifacts, and any exported report files.
7. Exercise failure and regression paths: empty meeting, low-confidence transcript, diarization disagreement, redacted transcript spans, deleted meeting/profile data, unsupported generated claims, missing owners/dates, and stale memory writes.
8. Fill `.github/issue-evidence/12499-meeting-intelligence-benchmark.md` or a successor artifact with links to every real artifact above, marking only truly non-applicable rows as `N/A - <reason>`.

## Work An Agent Can Still Do

- Validate the real manifest and generated `meeting-transcription-proof-report.json` once a human provides artifacts.
- Summarize live trajectory JSONL and compare observed scores against thresholds.
- Add regression fixtures from any failure found during the human run.
- Tighten deterministic scoring if manual review exposes a false positive or false negative.
- Update PR #13169 or a follow-up PR with evidence links and test adjustments.

## Done Criteria

- `generated_artifact_scores` contains all eight required rows with passing threshold-direction validation.
- Live-model rows include trajectory JSONL, raw prompt, model output, and judge output.
- Manual rows include reviewed notes tying generated artifacts to transcript spans.
- Real product evidence covers UI, logs, recordings, domain artifacts, failure paths, and regression tests.

topPRs.title: release: promote develop to main — billing fix, app-mode onboarding, sso, voice parity (+448 commits)
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
Production release: promotes `develop` → `main`, which deploys the Worker to `api.elizacloud.ai` and the Pages projects to the apex + `app.elizacloud.ai`.

## Why now

Headline fix: **half of all production inference requests fail** with "Billing authorization is warming up" — a strict success/failure alternation reproduced live (8-call probe: 4 ok / 4 warming; raw inference 0.49–1.48s throughout, so the model path is healthy and the auth gate is the defect). The fix (#17745, republish the org-balance gate hint after a debit) has been on `develop` since before this cycle; production is the only place it has not landed.

Also shipping, user-facing:
- **App-mode onboarding** (#17752): logging in on `app.elizacloud.ai` lands in *your* dedicated agent — automatic entry, chooser, resume, error fallback. Evidence: live before/after captures, walkthrough video, OCR review on the PR.
- **Cross-origin SSO** (#17788): one login across the dashboard and app origins — atomic single-use codes on Postgres, fail-closed logout, PKCE binding; hardened after security review.
- **Fired reminders deliver their content** (#17776), never a bare acknowledgement.
- **Node embedding sidecar** (#17787): provisioning installs it, health-checks probe it, self-heal converges the fleet — closing the "sidecars wiped again" regression loop.
- Latency hot-path work (#17743 lineage) and the rest of 448 commits of fixes.

Also shipping, operational: the certification pipeline itself was restored and made runnable (#17790, #17792, #17794, #17796–#17799, #17802 — the workflows had been deleted by an accidental sweep, and the chain had never run end to end; it now produces the signed certification this PR carries, and caught a real unlisted-public-route gap in review).

## Migrations (5 new, all additive + idempotent — audited)

| Migration | Shape |
|---|---|
| `0164_pooled_credentials` | 2 new tables + indexes, all `IF NOT EXISTS` |
| `0185_job_execution_interruptions` | `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (integer, default 0) |
| `0186_agent_sandbox_physical_name_indexes` | 2 partial indexes, `IF NOT EXISTS` |
| `0187_agent_sandbox_lifecycle_revision` | guarded column + `CREATE OR REPLACE` function + trigger replace (`DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` → recreate — idempotent pattern) |
| `0188_sso_bridge_store` | 2 new tables + index, all `IF NOT EXISTS` |

No destructive ops, no data rewrites, no `DELETE`/`TRUNCATE`/table drops anywhere in the set.

## Certification

`certification.json` at the repo root + signed evidence bundle at `evidence/bundle/`, produced by the `certification-hosted` workflow on the promoted commit: deterministic scenario lane (226 artifacts) + the develop-pr test recipe (`run-all-tests.mjs --only=test --no-cloud --concurrency=3`) recorded as the matrix lane, analyzed, rolled up, Ed25519-signed against the repo trust anchor, self-verified green before upload.

## Post-deploy verification (will be run and posted here)

1. Billing probe: 8 consecutive inference calls — expect 8/8 ok (was 4/8)
2. Latency: raw inference timing before/after
3. `/api/v1/admin/agent-image-canary` — expect present (was 404)
4. Control-plane deploy → sidecar self-heal converges all 8 nodes
5. Onboarding walk on app.elizacloud.ai + SSO bridge across origins


## Test proof at promotion (GitHub Actions major outage at promotion time)

The certified recipe (`build:core` + `build:views` + `run-all-tests.mjs --only=test --no-cloud --concurrency=4`) executed locally at `acf5fe75b4e` on the operator VPS: **123 package suites passed, 6 failed — every failure individually adjudicated, zero unexplained:**

| Local failure | Adjudication |
|---|---|
| app-core (guard) | REAL #17859 fallout: browser view missing from both desktop catalogs — **fixed in #17864** (8/8 green) |
| scenario-runner (guard) | REAL #17859 fallout: two new history-recall scenarios unclassified in the coverage map — **fixed in #17864** (17/17 green) |
| app-core (supervisor ×2) | environment-here: real-process spawn timeouts on this host; the robot certification run 31073689058 executed this exact suite green |
| vault | environment: headless host, no session bus ("keychain bypassed: host unsafe") — same class documented in #17818 |
| agent (early-logs) | environment: TTY color leak into captured stderr — documented in #17818 |
| plugin-calendar | environment: PGlite WASM init hook timeout under load — documented in #17818 |
| ui (flick + render bench) | environment: timing/benchmark under load; suites green across the PR gates that merged this code |

Every failing suite above is additionally green in GitHub's clean CI on the PRs that introduced this code. #17864 (two guard-map fixes, no runtime code) merges post-outage and rides the next promotion.

The signed certification re-dispatches the moment GitHub Actions recovers and lands as the allowed post-signing artifact. Deploy is dispatched on recovery (workflow_dispatch, environment=production).

topPRs.title: fix(app): land approved demo and runtime stack
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
> Release-candidate rollup (2026-08-06): exact head `1dcd08ba2e59f2fce29a1883fba5c14156e602c0`, tree `ba94bb6789acb2aa843939d6dbf7481c37d4e5c2`, 0 behind `develop@c765dee8b45eed092f6d70861536c27a7b5cde17`. This preserves 104 already-reviewed, dependency-ordered commits and excludes the two physical-LP3 tail PRs.

# Relates to

This rollup consolidates the exact published semantics from #17821, #17714, #17722, #17831, #17832, #17519, #17514, #17558, #17715, #17560, #17517, #17727, #17849, #17850, #17564, #17851, #17852, and #17853.

The scoped PRs remain open until this PR merges. Only after merge will they be closed as superseded, with this merged PR linked as the exact upstream replacement.

Definition of Done: full standard in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Why a rollup

The scoped branches form a linear dependency stack. Landing each one separately would repeatedly rewrite every descendant and run the same repository matrix approximately eighteen times. This PR retains the same commit and dependency order while giving GitHub one immutable, current-develop candidate to review and test.

No scoped work is discarded or flattened: all 104 commits remain individually inspectable.

# Dependency order preserved

1. Registry workspace dependency (#17821)
2. Deferred scheduling-before-calendar boot order (#17714)
3. Calendar dependency boundary (#17722)
4. Embedding capability/error boundary (#17831)
5. Trajectory bridge ownership (#17832)
6. Direct provider ownership (#17519)
7. Singular navigation replies (#17514)
8. Contextual view routing (#17558)
9. Canonical Notes/Calendar runtime and views (#17715)
10. Curated launcher (#17560)
11. Chat interactions and attachments (#17517)
12. Notification interaction fixes (#17727)
13. Approved UI/navigation polish (#17849)
14. Model-planned runtime cacheability (#17850)
15. Stage-1 history capability (#17564)
16. Browser surface and routing (#17851)
17. Integration coverage (#17852)
18. Final ripple/system integration coverage (#17853)

# Explicit exclusions

- #17688 and #17689 remain draft physical-LP3 tail PRs. They are not in this head and require real-device evidence.
- The Mac voice EOT/WAV fixes and native ABI15 submodule-pointer work are not in this head. They will ship as a separate, narrow voice stack after this product release candidate.
- No Cloud deployment, LP3 mutation, or device evidence is claimed here.

# What changes for users

- Notes, Calendar, Browser, launcher, chat, navigation, attachments, and notifications use their canonical current surfaces.

# Risks

This is broad in file count because it integrates a previously reviewed stack, not because it introduces a new monolithic implementation. Risk is controlled by the preserved commit boundaries, exact-head full repository verification, slice-specific focused suites, live model trajectories, browser/UI recordings, and the explicit exclusion of physical-device-only work.

ELIZA_SKIP_ARTIFACT_SYNC=1 bun install --frozen-lockfile

topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
# Fixes

Fixes #17868.

#17863 landed as `738d605ebc8aea093ab5fd38a40b12761f3b84a5`, providing the provider-independent private `VOICE_DM` response contract.

# What changed

- Replaces the Deepgram Flux realtime STT adapter with Cartesia Ink 2 while keeping Cartesia Sonic 3.5 for streamed TTS.
- Adds the local voice gateway used by the web preview to run Ink -> local elizaOS runtime/Cerebras -> Sonic without Eliza Cloud auth.
- Moves realtime ownership onto the always-mounted home `ChatOverlay` Talk control.
- Persists voice turns in canonical chat history, clears the composer after send, and keeps reconnect/resync state coherent.
- Keeps automatic TTS state in the composer waveform/Stop control and prevents message-action flashes.
- Prevents local runtime mode from booting an unrelated on-device text model.
- Preserves the mounted shell during background auth revalidation instead of flashing onboarding and rebuilding native listeners.
- Lets notifications use the actual space between the editorial header and composer, with directional overflow fades that remain correct in Android WebViews.

# Root cause

The provider gateway and visible composer had separate owners. The realtime hook was mounted in `ChatView`, but the product surface renders `ChatOverlay`, whose Talk control still invoked batch Cloud ASR. Message playback status also forced the action rail visible before Motion applied its hidden state.

For the LP3 notification regression, `HomeScreen` capped the list at an arbitrary 40% of a short viewport while the adjacent launcher region retained unused space. The shared scroll-fade fallback masked both edges unconditionally in WebViews, including the top edge at scroll start and lists with no hidden content.

# User impact

Talk now drives one continuous realtime flow from the actual composer. Transcript and response remain in the same conversation, TTS is interruptible, there is no duplicate mic, and fast turns do not flash message controls. On LP3-size screens the full available notification area is used and fades identify only content beyond the current scroll edge.

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): make sso bridge codes atomic and fail logout closed
topPRs.author: NubsCarson
topPRs.body:
> **Draft.** Backend, security, and behaviour work is complete and green, and the CI availability regression is fixed: fail-closed is now scoped to bridge-issued tokens (stamped with a `bridged: true` claim at /exchange re-mint), so ordinary session sync performs no datastore read at all - the pre-existing Redis-outage test passes unmodified, and a new suite proves a bridged token fails closed (503 `sso_unavailable`) during a marker-store outage. Remaining before undraft: the three surface-artifact rows (screenshots + walkthrough of the cross-origin flow), which need two live origins and are not faked here.

Security review of the dashboard/app SSO bridge found the single-use guarantee did not hold on the deployed cache and the logout marker failed open. This reworks the bridge onto a store that can actually deliver both, and closes four further findings.

## F1 (HIGH) — single-use codes were not atomic in production

The bridge claimed single-use via `cache.getAndDelete`, which on Cloudflare KV is a read-then-delete, not an atomic claim. `supportsAtomicOperations()` was never consulted, and the suite passed only because the mock was an atomic in-memory map. Two concurrent presenters of the same code could both be issued a session.

Codes now live in Postgres (`sso_bridge_codes`) and consumption is a single statement:

```sql
DELETE FROM sso_bridge_codes
 WHERE code_hash = $1 AND expires_at > now()
 RETURNING claims, challenge_hash
```

Exactly one of N concurrent presenters gets the row. Insert collision is a primary-key violation, so minting is atomically NX. Rows store `sha256(code)`, `sha256(verifier)`, and the **verified claims** — never a session JWT at rest; `/exchange` re-mints a fresh token from those claims, capped to the original token's `exp`.

This holds because KV is no longer in the path at all — the claim runs on the Worker's strongly-consistent Hyperdrive Postgres, the same store that already backs sessions and idempotency fences.

## F2 (HIGH) — logout marker failed open, and was invisible for ~60s

The marker was a cache key: a KV read miss during an outage read as "not logged out", and KV's propagation window meant a real logout stayed invisible to the paired origin. Both failure modes bridged a session that should have been dead.

The marker moves to Postgres (upsert with `GREATEST`, so it only moves forward). `isBlockedBySsoBridgeLogout` now **throws** on store failure and both bridge legs translate that into `503 sso_unavailable`, so the client falls back to per-origin login. An outage means no bridging — never "not logged out". Because codes and markers share one store, an outage that could lose a stamp also disables minting entirely.

## F3 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — dashboard sign-out never stamped, and the paired origin re-planted cookies

Three parts: both `ConsoleShell` sign-out branches now route through `signOutFromSsoBridgedHost`; `POST /api/auth/steward-session` refuses tokens issued at or before the marker with a distinct `401 session_ended`, killing the cookie re-plant server-side; and `StewardProviderRuntime` treats `session_ended` as a real revocation rather than a stale-proxy blip.

**Residual, documented in code:** the paired origin's raw bearer still works against the API until `exp`. Closing that needs a revocation lookup inside `verifyStewardTokenCached`, which is platform-wide and out of this PR's scope.

## F4/F5/F8 — binding and abuse surface

- **PKCE binding**: the app origin generates a verifier (sessionStorage only); `sha256(verifier)` travels as `challenge`. `/mint` requires it, `/exchange` requires the verifier. HTTP logs and history no longer contain enough to redeem a code.
- **Claim-then-verify**: the server consumes before checking the verifier, so every refusal path burns the code; the client also fires a verifier-less burn on state-mismatch. The mint leg requires `document.referrer` to be the paired origin, so a forced cross-site navigation cannot drive minting.
- **Origin gate**: the `Referer` fallback is removed — Origin-only, fail closed.

**F6** (plantable `steward-authed` hint) is documented as accepted risk: it is a routing hint only, loop-guarded to one bounce per tab per 5 minutes, and no unplantable cross-origin signal exists for a first visit. **F7** (logout CSRF) is pre-existing and flagged as follow-up.

## Migration

`0188_sso_bridge_store.sql` is hand-written, matching 0082–0187 in this repo (no drizzle snapshots since 0081).
